avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and pays for planting them on sidewalks, in parks and on private land. It also funds the machinery and employee teams that do this work in the boroughs. At the same time, borough councils allow construction projects to deviate from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.titre: Tree planting contracts on public land
etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees in seven boroughs, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included.

The City pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land until December 31, 2026. Pierrefonds-Roxboro, for its part, transfers $162,233.12 from the parks fund to buy trees and plants.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion on rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the 40 trees and 25% required. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini excavator-backhoe with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for blue-collar teams assigned to planting. Outremont awards the renovation of the chalet in parc Pratt and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, for an expense of $800,416.17, financed in part by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

The City leases plots in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for $100, so it can operate a transition nursery there. The lease runs for 24 months starting May 1, 2026, and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit a progress report on October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
The 855 trees in lot 2 must be planted in spring 2027; watering, maintenance and replacement continue until the end of November 2029.
The lease for the transition nursery ends on April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Contracts for snow removal and snow loading, abrasive spreading, and parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs mainly signed, extended and paid for contracts related to snow: turnkey snow removal from streets and sidewalks, rental of graders and loader-tractors with operators, vehicle towing, and spring street cleaning. Some boroughs also drew on their surpluses to cover expenses from the 2025-2026 winter, and others amended their by-laws covering contractors who clear snow from private lots.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie hired companies to maintain, clean, and clear snow from Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, square Victoria, and other sites. It also extended snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord approved extra spending for renting an additional grader, and Saint-Léonard allocated $200,000 from surplus to staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offered to have city council itself provide staff at the snow disposal site during loading.

The City extended turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro by twelve months, as well as towing contracts and equipment rentals with operators in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie and Anjou did the same for their loader-tractors and their grader.

Anjou amended the amount of fines under its by-law on snow removal from lots by contractors, and Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its by-law on snow removal and clearing. Saint-Léonard tabled a draft by-law requiring snow removal contractors working on industrial, commercial and institutional lots to hold a permit.

aSurveiller.texte: The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
Snow removal from roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City funds and carries out work on its water systems: rehabilitation of pipes in several boroughs, replacement of lead service connections and reconstruction of main pipes under downtown streets. It is also continuing the disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, including the construction of the oxygen production unit, and is contracting out the plant's routine maintenance to companies. It is passing loan by-laws to pay for this work.

etapes.texte: The City is increasing from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish building the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The City awards a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining them, without digging a trench, and to redo the roadway. The work affects streets in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest, Outremont, Verdun, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Saint-Léonard.

etapes.titre: Lead water service connections assigned to boroughs
etapes.texte: Boroughs offer the city council to carry out themselves the replacement of lead service connections, including the portion located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the owners.

The City awards contracts to rebuild a 500 mm water pipe along rue Guy and pipes on rue De Champlain, and to rehabilitate a 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord. It adds funds to the contracts for rue de la Cathédrale and rue Saint-Antoine Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer systems, announced for October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 expected starting the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Completion of the rue de la Cathédrale water pipe rehabilitation work pushed back from December 2026 to March 2027.
Rue Guy worksite expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant's ozone plant expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system rationalization.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail running through the park, with a footbridge of about 150 metres and a 12.7-hectare meadow [CG26 0121].

etapes.titre: Urban greenhouses entrusted to the borough
etapes.texte: The City approves a complex of research, training and community production greenhouses in the southwest sector of the park, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The agglomeration delegates the project to the city council, which accepts the offer of the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough to carry it out.

The borough awards a company the contract to redevelop rue De Louvain, between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62 [CA26 14 0076]. The work affects sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City awards a contract for the second phase of the electrical system rationalization work at the environmental complex: new power supply, transformer, backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture. It also entrusts two companies with the general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor at the environmental complex; the compost is used in particular for landscaping the park [CG26 0320]. The borough then awards a contract of $499,865.92 including taxes for the supply and installation of the greenhouses [CA26 14 0163].

etapes.titre: Snow removal and second funding request
etapes.texte: The City extends by six months the snow removal contract for the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium. The borough authorizes the filing of a funding request with the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, under the Véloce III program, for a bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, to which the City is submitting its request for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work is to be completed in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
The greenhouses are announced to come into service in winter 2027.
The extended snow removal covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027.
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, and 26 hectares will be added in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
The rue De Louvain construction project has one phase from May to October 2027 and another from May to August 2028.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is maintaining and protecting sections of the Grand parc de l'Ouest. It adjusted a contract for repairing heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, submitted an application for an international designation related to the night sky at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and had two sectors listed in a registry of protected natural areas. It also awarded contracts for culvert reconstruction, snow removal, tree felling, and housekeeping.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. Buried stones, extra mortar, and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase, according to file 1255414002.

The City submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. It commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping night-time access open to the public.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural areas
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans. Elected officials also review the 2025 report on the areas.

The City awards contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots at Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques, as well as housekeeping for nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, including the chalet d'accueil, the Maison Richer, and the Château Gohier.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Housekeeping of the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension to October 31, 2031.
Tree felling planned from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
For the night sky designation: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky's response expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming shelters and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations to shelter people experiencing homelessness during the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

etapes.titre: Warming shelters and outreach workers in boroughs
etapes.texte: Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two psychosocial outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is ratifying the continuation of a contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. to operate a warming shelter for the 2025-2026 winter.

etapes.titre: Financial support for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adding $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects focus on the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public spaces, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting out of the Bain Saint-Denis
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council is adopting a framework to receive private cash donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is transferring $250,000 for the fit-out work of the temporary warming shelter at the Bain Saint-Denis, and city council is adopting a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness.

etapes.titre: Encampments, support services and Nuit des sans-abri
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Mission Old Brewery a $149,520 contract to support people from the encampment area on rue Notre-Dame toward shelter and housing, and is paying $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee is authorizing an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling on the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne, and Ville-Marie is regulating noise for the event on October 16, 2026 on rue Beaudry.

aSurveiller.texte: The social brigade agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
The ruling on the merits of the dispute over the encampments at the viaduc Van Horne is expected in 2027, according to the file.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is leasing to the Société de transport de Montréal a 2,787-square-metre lot south of rue de Louvain, for parking for employees with a permit sticker, for $49,293 over three years. It is also leasing 836 square metres to a pay-by-app parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

etapes.titre: Temporary occupations of the Louvain Ouest lot
etapes.texte: The City is lending, free of charge, a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization for a vegetable garden, and two parcels totalling 3,316 square metres to another organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. The borough is paying $35,000 to an organization for the Esplanade-Louvain temporary space at 150 rue de Louvain Ouest, is authorizing an event-related use on the vacant lot, and city council is taking charge of an activation lease on 78,244 square feet.

etapes.titre: The main street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The file states that the first residential project is under construction and that addresses need to be assigned in the short term.

The City is awarding a company a contract worth $10,311,940.25 including taxes to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the remediation of the soil at the former gas station, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net to the infrastructure department's budget.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It is also adopting a draft by-law setting the height limit at 73 metres on part of the municipal lot, at the corner of avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on rue de Louvain Est continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, planting).
The response from the Ministère des Transports to the request for financial assistance is expected in fall 2026.
The loan of the lot for the greenhouse and sunflowers runs until October 31, 2027; the one for the vegetable garden, until December 31, 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site still need to be named before development is complete, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City is adjusting its residual materials collections: new days and new frequencies in several boroughs, bin purchases, resident support. It is extending contracts for food waste treatment, container collection and ecocentre service, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling its annual reports and inspector general reports on collection subcontracting.

etapes.texte: The executive committee changes the days, schedules and collection sectors in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31, and the division of sectors 41 and 42 changes starting May 1, 2026.

The City extends its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. twice, by six months each time, to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration, at an additional cost of $3,269,055.43 taxes included per extension [CG26 0045]. It explains that the start-up of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre is not confirmed and that it can end the contracts with 30 days' notice [CG26 0417].

The City enters into framework agreements to supply brown bins and garbage bins, then others to supply and distribute garbage bins in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where collection will be spaced out in two phases, fall 2026 and fall 2027 [CM26 0690]. Ahuntsic-Cartierville entrusts Ville en vert with an information and awareness mandate, and the executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations during neighbourhood festivals.

etapes.titre: Containers, ecocentres and former dump sites
etapes.texte: The City extends by 12 months the front-loading and semi-underground container collection contracts awarded to Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions, as well as the container contract for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre transferred to GFL Environmental inc. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract of $734,690.25 taxes included to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres [CG26 0416], extends the dumping authorization management software, and retains two firms for studies related to construction on former disposal sites.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of food waste treatment by Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. runs until February 28, 2027.
Container collection and the Saint-Laurent ecocentre container service are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The loan of dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The dumping authorization software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply in the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. This year, it obtained from the Québec government an additional delay to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for the water supply system and public domain, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. It is also leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Extended delay to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The City approves the addendum to the 2017 transfer deed, with no financial compensation.

The City guarantees a loan of $2,000,000 granted by the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, city council rejects an opposition motion on governance and asset management in the sector.

etapes.titre: Two loans for the water supply system and streets
etapes.texte: The City adopts a loan of $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil, sewers, water supply, streets, land purchases. It also adopts a loan of $12,000,000 to build water main pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

The City leases parcels of the site to three organizations for $100 or $200 in rent: urban agriculture with MultiCaf and with Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora, a transition nursery with Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain.

The City transfers, at no cost, to the organization Communia a vacant piece of land of 4,777.7 square metres in the southeast part of the former racetrack, to build at least 225 non-market housing units there. It repeals the 2025 agreement with another organization and authorizes a depreciation expense of $877,488.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline granted to the City to complete the sale of a first piece of land on the site.
2031: date by which the infrastructure must be completed, according to the condition of the federal grant cited in the loan by-laws.
April 30, 2027: end of the urban agriculture lease with MultiCaf.
March 31, 2028: end of the extended lease of Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora. April 30, 2028: end of the transition nursery lease.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City funded studies, awarded design contracts and launched park redevelopment work in several boroughs, from Le Sud-Ouest to Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, as well as Verdun, LaSalle and Saint-Laurent. It also adjusted contracts already underway when contaminated soil or unexpected construction issues extended the work. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it repaired infrastructure, awarded routine maintenance work and submitted a candidacy for an international designation related to the night sky.

etapes.texte: The City awarded the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It also gave money to Verdun for soil studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, accepted an amount from Hydro-Québec for phase 4 of parc d'Argenson, and authorized a public art competition at parc des Eaux-Cachées.

etapes.titre: Work and maintenance in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City awarded a contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, in the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub. It also awarded contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots, the felling of ash trees and declining trees, and housekeeping services for nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector.

etapes.titre: New projects and land transferred to park use
etapes.texte: Other redevelopment contracts were awarded: parcs Denise-Morelle and Baldwin in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, parc J.O.R.-Leduc in LaSalle and parc Aimé-Caron in Saint-Laurent. The City also removed a portion of street from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requested the same change for a 75.2-square-metre strip at parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: The snow removal contract for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Housekeeping services for nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector run from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with an option to extend for 12 months.
For the DarkSky candidacy, the lighting management plan must be submitted in February 2027, and the response is expected in April 2027.
For the parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: the winner will be chosen in October 2026, the contract awarded in December 2026, and the artwork installed in 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027.
Work on parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, must be completed by June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares: it adopts funding rules, pays out money to boroughs and business development corporations, then closes street sections to cars and regulates sales, noise and traffic on these streets. It also settles a dispute related to the development of a public square, changes the status of a piece of land, and gives a name to a square.

etapes.titre: Funding rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to the work on a public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

Boroughs close street sections to cars and authorize terraces, the sale of food and drinks, music and ground painting: Ville-Marie for thirteen streets, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce for the Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison, Outremont for avenue Bernard, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for rue Ontario Est, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal for avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth.

The executive committee grants $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026 during the FIFA World Cup. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce closes avenue de Monkland for a commercial promotion from August 20 to 23, 2026, and Ville-Marie authorizes a musical sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles.

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council names "place Chez-Marguerite" the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque, in Montréal-Nord, and changes the status of a 899 square metre piece of land from street to local park near the Langelier metro station. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal reviews the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal in three sections.

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Traffic resumes on the chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp on November 1, 2026, after dismantling on November 1 and 2.
The ordinance on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transport contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the 2027 edition will take place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed.
Support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe continues until December 31, 2028: $22,500 in 2027 and $20,000 in 2028.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of an officer
etapes.texte: The City adopts a loan by-law of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys patrol motorcycles, replaces the oil heating of the cavalry building at 1515, chemin Remembrance, and extends the housekeeping of its headquarters. It also awards meals for detained persons to a new company and extends the software maintenance of the call dispatch system.

etapes.titre: Leases for neighbourhood police stations and premises
etapes.texte: The City renews the leases of neighbourhood police station 15, rue de l'Église in Verdun, and neighbourhood police station 26, avenue Mountain Sights. It also rents 50 parking spaces at 260, boulevard De Maisonneuve and extends the lease of the SPVM training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier in Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day of the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood police station 46, for which the Anjou borough bought tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the ten-year lease of the metro unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: delivery deadline for the port patrol boat and its trailer.
September 30, 2027: expected end of the work to replace the oil heating of the cavalry building.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and borrowings of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), and sells, leases or loans it land for its stations, ventilation buildings and staff. It also oversees metro worksites and bus stops on its territory, and entrusts the STM with municipal work related to the extension of the blue line. Borough councils and city council adopt motions on the development of the network.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville establishes and removes bus waiting posts as part of the network redesign, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks for the new stops. Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and redo the vault of the green line tunnel 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026; the City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation building in Outremont, adds an incidental budget to the Berri-UQAM station worksite, and does not oppose the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It then concludes 72-month framework agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for the design, technical assistance and impact management of the redevelopment of the blue line corridor.

The agglomeration approves STM borrowings and amends its capital works program: analysis of the replacement of MR-73 railcars, extension of their service life, bus priority measures, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, refurbishment of surface buildings, and technological and security risk management.

City council asks Québec to study the conditions for keeping the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line in Montréal. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Greater South-West, while Anjou asks the STM to stop the study of a reserved lane on rue Beaubien and avenue du Val-d'Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: Approval from the ministère des Affaires municipales expected in November 2026 for borrowings related to MR-73 railcars and the refurbishment of surface buildings.
Work on the Rielle ventilation building, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is expected in 2031.

velo.titre: Bikes: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are building and repairing bike lanes, regulating car traffic around them, and buying equipment for the BIXI system. Work affects the REV Lajeunesse, rue Saint-Jacques, avenue Christophe-Colomb, and corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. The City is also settling its rent with Hydro-Québec for land used for bike paths and is asking Québec for financial help for four new projects.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes a $100,000 expense, taxes included, for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is renting a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is imposing mandatory manoeuvres on drivers on avenue Christophe-Colomb and is officializing the bike lanes between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse. Outremont is tabling a draft by-law to turn a shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path, and Ville-Marie is making rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound between Peel and Robert-Bourassa for a section of the REV.

The City is awarding PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61, taxes included, for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI, then a $394,851.17 contract, taxes included, to Laser AMP for the stations' steel bases. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and the Sud-Ouest are each including the installation of a BIXI station in street and laneway projects.

City council is approving a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on land owned by Hydro-Québec used for bike paths, parks and gardens. It is then approving a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a strip of about 366 square metres used as a bike path in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial help from Québec
etapes.texte: The City is authorizing the filing of four requests for financial assistance to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build bike lanes and sidewalks on rue de Champlain, rue Saint-Jacques, rue Guy and rue Laurier. It is committing to pay at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: The new traffic directions and lane assignments on rue Saint-Jacques, related to the REV, take effect on November 6, 2026.
The lease for the bike path land rented from Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until December 31, 2035.
